newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips shares surge 5 pct to record high.
newsitem.headline: Philips shares surge 5 pct to record high.

text.p: Shares in Philips Electronics NV jumped 4.70 guilders or 5.5 percent to a record high 90.40 guilders on Tuesday, climbing in a sharply higher Amsterdam stock market on the view that the shares remain undervalued.

Analysts said recent restructuring measures introduced by new chairman Cor Boonstra appeared to be paying off and that steep extraordinary costs would not be needed in the future as non-performing businesses were being successfully removed.
"Philips shares should easily see the 100 guilders within the next few months," said ABN AMRO analyst Corneille Couwenberg. "We see further upside in the longer run."

"The share will see a rerating because Mr Boonstra has reduced exposure to a lot of loss-making operations and will therefore need fewer extraordinary restructuring costs," he said, adding this would boost future profits.

Analysts have long been forecasting that 1997 would show a strong improvement on 1996, which saw a bottom line net loss of 590 million guilders as net restructuring charges of 1.3 billion guilders bit deep.
Philips shares, which started the year at 68.40 guilders, have bounded up from 76.50 guilders on February 13, the day it announced the 1996 loss.
Analysts said Philips shares had started to move as the Amsterdam bourse was offering fewer and fewer clear-cut buying opportunities as it climbs back towards record highs.
"People have taken the time to look at the results and read buy notes from analysts," said Couwenberg. "They're looking for companies which still have the potential to rise.
"It's getting increasingly difficult to see which stocks are worth buying at these historically high stock market levels."
